title: Sidewalk
description: Your walk to work, rain or shine.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not yet. The screen at the bus stop says it's five minutes late.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thank goodness. I ran all the way from the crosswalk.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You should have waited for the traffic light. That van almost hit you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I know, I know. I'll be more careful tomorrow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Here it comes. Have you got your bus pass ready?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wow, it's really coming down now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Come and stand under my umbrella until it eases off.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thanks. Let's wait under the store sign over there. It's a bit drier.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good idea. And watch out for that puddle by the curb.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Too late. My shoes are already soaked.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let's grab a hot coffee inside while we wait.

selfTalk.text: The store sign on the corner is so bright that I can see it from the end of the block.
If I'm early, I'll stop at the convenience store under that sign and grab a coffee.
I've walked past that store sign every morning for a year, and I still don't know what the logo means.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is the convenience store under that green sign open this early?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's open 24 hours. The sign stays on all night.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Great, I need to pick up some breakfast on the way to work.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Try the egg sandwiches. They've just added them to the menu.

selfTalk.text: The bike lane is painted bright green so that drivers can't pretend they didn't see it.
I'm going to ride in the bike lane today instead of squeezing between the buses.
It really annoys me when delivery vans park in the bike lane and I have to swerve into traffic.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you cycle to work now? I saw you in the bike lane yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yeah, ever since they opened the new bike lane, it's actually faster than the bus.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Isn't it dangerous during rush hour?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not really. As long as cars stay out of it, I feel pretty safe.

selfTalk.text: The curb on this side of the street is so high that people with suitcases always struggle with it.
I'll wait on the curb until the light changes instead of stepping into the road too early.
I almost tripped over the curb this morning because I was looking at my phone instead of the street.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Watch out, the curb is really high right here.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thanks! I nearly twisted my ankle on it last week.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It's even worse when it rains, because the gutter fills up with water.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I usually cross a bit further down, where the curb is lower.

selfTalk.text: The streetlight outside my building is still on, even though the sun came up an hour ago.
I'm going to report the broken streetlight so the city can fix it before winter.
Walking home is a lot less scary now that they've put a new streetlight on this corner.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Have you noticed that the streetlight by the bus stop keeps flickering?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, it's been like that for weeks. It went out completely last night.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Someone should call the city about it.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I already did. They said they'd send someone to replace the bulb by Friday.

selfTalk.text: The bus stop on my street has a glass roof, but the rain still blows in from the side.
I'd better leave five minutes early so I can get to the bus stop before the 8:15 comes.
I always feel a little anxious at the bus stop when the screen says the next bus is delayed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Does the number 12 still stop here? The bus stop sign looks new.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: They moved it last month. The 12 stops across the street now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oh, no wonder I've been waiting for twenty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Lots of people have made the same mistake. They should really put up a notice.

selfTalk.text: The traffic light at this corner stays red for so long that people start crossing anyway.
I'll press the button and wait until the traffic light turns green before I cross.
Whenever a traffic light changes just as I reach it, I feel like the whole city is against me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: This traffic light takes forever, doesn't it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It does. I think it's timed for cars, not for people on foot.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we just cross? There aren't any cars coming.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'd rather wait. There's a police officer right over there.

selfTalk.text: The trash can next to the bus stop is overflowing again because nobody emptied it over the weekend.
I'll hold on to my coffee cup until I find a trash can that isn't completely full.
It drives me crazy when people leave their garbage on the ground right next to an empty trash can.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is there a trash can around here? I need to throw away this wrapper.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There's one by the bus stop, but it's probably full.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ugh, it always is in the mornings.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: The garbage truck doesn't come until noon, so it fills up fast.

selfTalk.text: The man next to me is holding a huge red umbrella that's big enough for two people.
I'm going to keep a folding umbrella in my bag, so I'm never caught in the rain again.
If I leave my umbrella on the bus one more time, I'm going to stop buying nice ones.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oh no, it's starting to pour, and I left my umbrella at home.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Here, you can share mine. It's big enough for both of us.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you sure? I don't want you to get wet.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's fine. We're walking the same way anyway.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thanks, you're a lifesaver. I'll buy you a coffee next time.

selfTalk.text: There's a short red fire hydrant on the sidewalk that I've bumped into at least twice.
I'll park a little further down, because I don't want a ticket for blocking the fire hydrant.
As a kid, I loved summer days when the firefighters opened the hydrant and we all played in the water.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You can't park there. That's right in front of a fire hydrant.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Really? I didn't even see it behind those bags.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yeah, my brother got a huge ticket for doing the same thing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thanks for warning me. I'll find another spot.

selfTalk.text: Someone has parked an orange scooter right in the middle of the sidewalk, so everyone has to walk around it.
Once I get my license, I'm going to ride a scooter to work instead of waiting for the bus.
I get a bit nervous when a scooter zooms past me on the sidewalk without slowing down.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is that your new scooter? It looks great.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thanks! I bought it last month, and it's already saved me so much time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Isn't it hard to find parking downtown?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not at all. That's the best thing about a scooter. It fits almost anywhere.

selfTalk.text: The stripes on this crosswalk have faded so much that some drivers don't notice it at all.
I'm going to walk to the crosswalk instead of running across the road like I usually do.
I feel a lot safer when drivers actually stop and wait for me at the crosswalk.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Let's cross here. It's quicker.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'd rather use the crosswalk. The cars come around that corner really fast.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You're right. It's only a few more steps anyway.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: And the walk signal is already on, so we won't have to wait.

selfTalk.text: There's a round metal manhole cover in the road that rattles loudly every time a truck drives over it.
I'll step around the manhole cover, because it gets really slippery when it rains.
I've always wondered what's under a manhole cover, but I'm not brave enough to find out.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you hear that loud clank just now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's that manhole cover. Every bus that goes over it makes the same noise.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It's a bit loose, isn't it? Someone could get hurt.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I think road workers are coming to fix it next week.
